newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on healthy demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on healthy demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were assessed steady to firm as local buying interest remained healthy but weak crude values might limit the climb, traders said.

High sulphur fuel oil, 180-cst prices were assessed at $124/$126 per tonne. An offer was seen by a major for January 14-19 loading at $127 per tonne late Friday but traders expected offers to come down to Thrusday's level of $125.

A Venezuelan cargo of 380-cst was expected to arrive by January. Traders said the market for 180-cst was tight as gas oil, the cutterstock used to reduce the viscosity of 380-cst to 180-cst, was still expensive.
Pockets of Chinese demand were seen. Some discussion were heard that freight rates between South Korea and China were easing from $8.00 per tonne to just around $7.60-$7.90 per tonne.
Traders said inventories remained low in Singapore, citing the fall Thursday in residue stocks figures from the Singapore's Trade Development Board.
A local trader who had purchased a 20,000 tonnes of January fuel oil at $125 per tonne said he was still interested to buy but could not provide further details.
Swaps levels firm slightly. January were quoted at $120.25/$121.25, around 25 cents lower from Thursday's indications.
